Present Continuous vs Be Going to in Affirmative

You can use the “present continuous tense” to talk about actions that are happening in a precise moment in the present. On the other hand, you use “be going to” to express intentions in the immediate future.

To create an affirmative statement in the“present continuous tense” you need to use the auxiliary verb to be and the main verb in –ing form.

Structure:

Subject+auxiliary verb to be+ main verb + ing + complement

Example:
We are securing all data in our company.

On the other hand, to create an affirmative statement with "be going to" you need to use the auxiliary verb to be, going to and the main verb in its base form.

Structure:

Subject +auxiliary verb to be + going to + main verb in base form + complement

Example:
Our engineers are going to send a report later.
It means that all people who are working within computing environments can have access to all system files from the company.

Preposition + Ing
Whenever you use a verb after some prepositions you need to include -ing in the verb.
These are the prepositions that you can use with the -ing form.

Andrea: Hi, Jimmy! So, today I'm going to explain to you something important about data security. I understand you are going to be in charge of the personnel area, right?
Jimmy: Yes, I am. I'm working with that area.
Andrea: Ok, perfect! I'm going to start by telling you why it is important for us the data security in all of our areas. As you know, this company possesses a multiuser network system. It means that all people who are working within computing environments can have access to all system files from the company. In this way, it's vital for us to determine different users' status for each employee in here. So, for example, you receive an administrator status that will allow you to have access to important data in your area, but at the same time, you will have restrictions to access other available data in the network. This is one of the most useful security mechanisms to avoid data breaches.

Jimmy: Why is it important to secure data?
Andrea: Because either people or a malicious program can steal or even destroy important information or system files from the company just by accessing them from other portals. For example, I know that universities and financial institutions are constantly facing data theft. Also, viruses can be loaded to those files what it will be a difficult situation for us.

Jimmy: Why are we securing data in this company?
Andrea: Because we are managing some important information from other companies. At this moment, we're developing an encryption code which consists in protecting valuable data from reading by encoding its content. Finally, remember that employees can only have access to files that you share as public or that they create. If by any chance you need someone to work on a file that is restricted, you can give them permissions for working with those files.
Jimmy: I understand, thanks for explaining!
Andrea: No problem! Let's check the username you are going to use.
